name: Linguistically Motivated MT Metrics Challenge Set
description: We employ a linguistically motivated challenge set in order to evaluate the state-of-the-art machine translation metrics submitted to the Metrics Shared Task of the 7th Conference for Machine Translation. The challenge set includes about 20,000 items extracted from 145 MT systems for two language directions (German-English, English-German), covering more than 100 linguistically-motivated phenomena organized in 14 categories. The best performing metrics are YiSi-1, BERTScore and COMET-22 for German-English, and UniTE, UniTE-ref, XL-DA and xxl-DA19 for English-German.Metrics in both directions are performing worst when it comes to named-entities & terminology and particularly measuring units. Particularly in German-English they are weak at detecting issues at punctuation, polar questions, relative clauses, dates and idioms. In English-German, they perform worst at present progressive of transitive verbs, future II progressive of intransitive verbs, simple present perfect of ditransitive verbs and focus particles.
reputation: A well-regarded WMT challenge-set used by the MT and metrics research community to probe linguistic phenomena; commonly cited in metric-evaluation work.
notes: Small, targeted challenge set focusing on specific linguistic phenomena; evaluates metrics rather than end-to-end MT systems, so it is not representative of overall translation quality. Primarily used for diagnostic/analysis purposes rather than large-scale benchmarking.
